pubflow

pubflow (“publishing workflow”) is the companion package of pipeflow (>= 0.5.0.9028). pipeflow computes; pubflow covers everything around a pipeline that is needed to publish its results:

  • Parameters: self-describing parameter objects with validity checks and configs;
  • Parameter UI: a Shiny module that builds inputs from a pipeline’s parameters, with per-field validation;
  • Outputs and documents: conventions for step outputs (tables, figures, Markdown text) and layout steps that arrange them into documents;
  • Viewer: a Shiny module that shows a document as one scrollable page;
  • Reports: HTML, Word (DOCX) and PDF via Pandoc, with traceability and DOCX post-processing.

Status

Under development towards v0.1. The design is in dev/DESIGN.md, the open work in dev/PLAN.md.

Example

A step returns a table, a layout step arranges it into a document, and pub_render() writes the document to a Word file:

library(pipeflow)
library(pubflow)

pip <- pip_new("my-pip") |>
    pip_add("fit", function(data = airquality, xVar = "Temp") {
        coefs <- coef(lm(paste("Ozone ~", xVar), data = data))
        data.frame(term = names(coefs), estimate = unname(coefs))
    }) |>
    pip_add("table", function(fit = ~fit) {
        pub_table(fit, caption = "Linear model of the ozone concentration",
                  digits = c(estimate = 3L))
    }) |>
    pip_add("report", function(table = ~table) {
        pub_doc(pub_section("Results", table), title = "Ozone in New York")
    })
pip_run(pip)
pub_render(pip[["report", "out"]], "docx")

The vignette vignette("v01-get-started", package = "pubflow") goes through the whole flow: params, outputs, documents, report files and a Shiny app.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rpahl/pubflow")

System requirements: pandoc >= 3.6; for PDF output xelatex (default) or typst. pubflow finds pandoc via the environment variable PUBFLOW_PANDOC, then RSTUDIO_PANDOC, then the PATH; typst via PUBFLOW_TYPST, then the PATH, then the typst bundled with Quarto. PDF via xelatex needs the LaTeX packages of huxtable (huxtable::install_latex_dependencies()) and pdflscape, fancyhdr, lastpage, float and newunicodechar (TinyTeX: tinytex::tlmgr_install(c("pdflscape", "fancyhdr", "lastpage", "float", "newunicodechar"))); pandoc finds xelatex on the PATH.

Word reference documents

DOCX output uses pubflow’s reference document (inst/templates/reference.docx, built by data-raw/reference_docx.R). Its styles and the bookmarks of the header and footer lines that your own reference document must provide are listed in vignette("v06-reports", package = "pubflow").

Development

The development library is managed with renv for R 4.5.3; start R in the repository root and run renv::restore() once. R >= 4.3 is supported and checked on CI.

R -q -e "devtools::document()"
R -q -e "devtools::test()"
R -q -e "pkgload::load_all(quiet = TRUE); lintr::lint_package()"
R -q -e "rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = '--no-manual', error_on = 'warning', check_dir = 'check')"
